woodPelletProfiles.name: 100% Shagbark Hickory Commercial Hardwood Pellets (High Lignin, Heavy Smoke)
woodPelletProfiles.description: Standard high-intensity hardwood for commercial pit barbecue. High lignin content delivers dense aromatic smoke (syringol and guaiacol) but generates elevated levels of Benzo[a]pyrene and Phenanthrene under oxygen-starved smoldering conditions.

woodPelletProfiles.name: Texas Post Oak Commercial Hardwood Pellets (Balanced Lignin, Clean Pyrolysis)
woodPelletProfiles.description: Widely utilized for commercial brisket smoking. Possesses lower extractive resin and lignin than hickory, yielding a cleaner combustion plume with reduced intermediate soot nucleation and lower submicron PAH aerosol condensations.

woodPelletProfiles.name: 100% Honey Mesquite Commercial Hardwood Pellets (Ultra-High Lignin & Tannins)
woodPelletProfiles.description: Aggressive combustion profile with high thermal release and heavy polyaromatic hydrocarbon formation. Pyrolyzes with dense soot particulate plumes that rapidly condense BaP and Chrysene onto cooler meat surfaces.

woodPelletProfiles.name: Orchard Applewood Commercial Fruitwood Pellets (High Hemicellulose, Low Resin)
woodPelletProfiles.description: Favored for poultry, pork ribs, and delicate charcuterie. Lower lignin percentage significantly diminishes the HACA ring-growth mechanism, resulting in lower total EFSA 4 PAH yields in the combustion effluent.

woodPelletProfiles.name: Substandard Construction Softwood/Pine Pellets (High Resins & Turpenes - Prohibited)
woodPelletProfiles.description: Contaminated or non-food-grade softwood pellets containing high abietic acid resins. Generates dense carcinogenic creosote, massive Chrysene and Fluoranthene emissions, and violates NFPA 96 / FDA food contact smoking mandates.

smokerArchitectures.name: Industrial Multi-Zone Continuous Wire Mesh Conveyor Smoker (60 ft, Dual Auger Burners)
smokerArchitectures.burners: Dual 350,000 BTU/hr Automated Pellet Pyrolyzers with Forced-Draft Fans
smokerArchitectures.sparkArrestorType: UL 1046 Stainless Steel Heavy Baffle with Automated Deluge Quench
smokerArchitectures.description: High-throughput commercial processing smoker for national barbecue and packaged meats. Features multi-zone temperature controls, automated oxygen-trim pellet combustion pots, and high-velocity convective draft circulation.

smokerArchitectures.name: Commercial Rotary Shelf Carousel Conveyor Smoker (16-Spit, 1,200 lb Capacity)
smokerArchitectures.sparkArrestorType: UL 1046 Baffle Filter with Cold Water Mist Header
smokerArchitectures.description: Standard production unit for high-volume smokehouse restaurants. Rotating racks ensure uniform thermal contact, while variable pellet auger feed adjusts smoke density across 4 to 12 hour smoking schedules.

smokerArchitectures.name: Compact Electric-Auger Continuous Conveyor Charcuterie Smoker (12 ft, 350 lb/day)
smokerArchitectures.burners: Single 65,000 BTU/hr Precision Micro-Auger Pellet Burner
smokerArchitectures.description: Designed for gourmet butcher shops and small smokehouses producing artisan sausages, jerky, and smoked cheese. Relies on low-temperature indirect smoke generation to preserve volatile terpenes.

smokerArchitectures.name: Unmaintained 90-Day Soot-Choked Conveyor Smoker (Flue Glazed Creosote, Flue Air Starved)
smokerArchitectures.burners: Fouled Auger Burner with Clinker-Choked Firepot (Incomplete Combustion)
smokerArchitectures.sparkArrestorType: Partially Missing / Tar-Clogged Wire Mesh Screen
smokerArchitectures.description: Severe fire and toxicological liability. Airflow is restricted by dense creosote in flue stack; smoldering firepot operates under heavy oxygen starvation, maximizing PAH formation and presenting imminent chimney autoignition risk.

pahCongenerProfiles.formationMechanism: Formed via HACA ring closure from phenanthryl and cyclopentadienyl radicals during sub-stoichiometric wood pyrolysis above 400°C.
Readily condenses onto soot particulates; ubiquitous indicator of incomplete biomass combustion.
Formed alongside chrysene from thermal fragmentation of lignocellulose and recombination of alkyl radicals.
Five-membered ring closure formed in high-heat firepot zones; strongly bound to carbonaceous soot particles.

regulatoryStandards.title: Maximum Levels for Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons in Traditionally Smoked Meats
regulatoryStandards.efsa4SumLimit: 12.0 μg/kg (ppb) wet weight (Sum of BaP, CHR, BaA, BbF)
regulatoryStandards.scope: Enforces mandatory laboratory HPLC-MS testing on commercial smoked meats, hams, sausages, and poultry.

regulatoryStandards.title: Solid Fuel Commercial Cooking Operations
regulatoryStandards.keyRequirement: Solid fuel cooking equipment shall have separate and dedicated exhaust systems, independent of all other cooking equipment flues. Spark arrestors must be UL 1046 listed and accessible for daily inspection.
regulatoryStandards.inspectionFrequency: Monthly manual scraping and inspection of flue plenum when burning solid wood fuels.

regulatoryStandards.title: Semivolatile Organic Compounds & PAHs by Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS)
regulatoryStandards.keyRequirement: Standard analytical methodology for measuring polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon concentrations in food matrices and industrial stationary combustion exhaust emissions.

regulatoryStandards.title: Coal Tar Pitch Volatiles / Particulate Polycyclic Organic Matter (PPOM)
regulatoryStandards.limit: 8-hour TWA PEL of 0.2 mg/m³ for benzene-soluble PPOM in commercial smokehouse worker breathing zones.

combustionCreosoteStages.structure: Dry, powdery, velvet-black soot easily swept with a wire brush.
combustionCreosoteStages.description: Forms when high draft velocity maintains chimney walls above the condensation point of pyroligneous acids.

combustionCreosoteStages.structure: Sticky, tar-like chips and porous carbonaceous crusted blisters.
combustionCreosoteStages.description: Formed when wood pellet moisture and condensed volatile wood alcohols mix with carbon particulate soot.

combustionCreosoteStages.structure: Dense, glassy, pitch-black rock-hard enamel welded to duct steel.
combustionCreosoteStages.description: Virtually impossible to sweep mechanically; auto-ignites at 450°C (842°F) creating an uncontrollable 1,100°C (2,000°F) structural flue chimney fire.
